question: Which host-lint release introduced the --docs repo-wide prose lane, and which rule source does that lane consult? Name the version and the rule source.

answer.rule_source: VOCABULARY.md §6 — "Prose agentic tells (advisory): a token-free trope adaptation" (the tropes.fyi adaptation carried by host-grammar's `tells` module)

sources.quote: ### D1: `--docs`, a repo-wide prose mode over authored docs *(host-lint, shipped v0.8.0)*
sources.locator: plan/0030 README — "## Deliverables" section, the "### D1" heading (milestone that specifies the `--docs` lane)

sources.quote: host-lint 0.8.0: --docs repo-wide prose lane, plus located, fix-hinted, tiered output
sources.locator: commit JSON — `commit.message`, first line (subject) of commit e652ffc, the tagged v0.8.0 commit whose Cargo.toml diff bumps 0.7.0 -> 0.8.0 and whose src/main.rs patch adds run_docs and the `--docs` flag
release JSON for tag v0.8.0 — top-level tag_name / target_commitish / name fields (same object reports "published_at":"2026-06-21T23:45:23Z")

sources.quote: // `--docs` is the repo-wide prose lane — the counterpart to the naming `--all`.
sources.locator: src/main.rs at tag v0.8.0 — comment block immediately above `fn run_docs`, whose loop filters to `.md` and calls `scan_prose_text(&content, rel, matches)`

sources.quote: The engine lives in `host-grammar` and runs on titles and drafts (`--stdin`) and on documents (`--prose`, `--docs`); `--all` runs both the naming and the prose lane over the tracked-doc set, so one command matches the host-lifecycle gate. See [VOCABULARY.md](VOCABULARY.md) §6.
sources.locator: host-lint README (main) — "What It Detects" section, closing paragraph of the prose agentic tells block

sources.quote: ## 6. Prose agentic tells (advisory): a token-free trope adaptation
sources.locator: VOCABULARY.md at tag v0.8.0 — section 6 heading; its opening paragraph adds "It lives in `host-grammar`'s `tells` module and host-lint calls it."
